html:
The Kingdom of the Aurès was a Berber kingdom in the Aurès mountains of eastern Algeria, from the late 5th century to about 703. It is shown here in 700, at its last stand.

The Aurès is a high, rugged massif, a natural fortress. Its Berber rulers broke away from the Vandals in the 480s and later held out against the Byzantines. In the late 7th century it became the centre of resistance to the Arab conquest. After the Berber leader Kusaila died, a woman led the fight: Dihya, known to Arab writers as al-Kahina, "the prophetess". She defeated the Umayyad general Hassan ibn al-Numan around 698.

Hassan came back with a larger army, and Dihya was killed in battle around 701 to 703. The region then came under the Umayyad Caliphate. The Chaoui Berbers of the Aurès still remember her as a heroine.
